newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to restructure its National Oil Company.
newsitem.headline: Romania to restructure its National Oil Company.

text.p: The Romanian government has decided to restructure the state National Oil Company (CRP) and bring it in line with Western standards, in a bid to streamline its oil sector, an official said on Monday.
"Our plan is to dissolve the CRP and replace it with a company similar in structure with Shell or Amoco. It's time for a change," said the official, who asked not to be named.
The CRP holding now groups 10 refineries, four transport and 41 oil distribution companies as well as a research institute and an oil exploration company.
Under the plan, the firms within the holding would split into independent commercial companies starting July 1, the official said.
He said the new firm to replace the CRP would include the Rafirom Bucuresti SA firm, Peco SA petroleum products retailer and Petrotrans Ploiesti SA oil transport company.
"The new company will be involved mainly in the processing of the locally-produced crude oil," the official said.
Its installed processing capacity would amount to some 10 million tonnes of crude oil per year, which is a realistic level for Romania's needs, sources in the oil sector said.
Last year, Romania's crude oil output amounted to some 6.8 million tonnes.

When CRP was created in 1995, authorities believed they could provide funds to import crude oil badly needed by Romania's industrial and energy sectors as well as streamline the exploration, refining, distribution and transport of oil.
But the company came under attack from private firms in the oil sector which accused CRP of alleged monopolistic practices.
Romania's refining industry, with a capacity of 34 million tonnes and developed during the rule of late dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, is the largest in central and eastern Europe.
